claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi-based alloy containing approximately 2 at.% Ti and 1 at.% Zr is single phase.
Rapid quenching from the homogenization temperature will freeze short-range-order clusters into the matrix.
Annealing at approximately 600°C for 1 hour followed by cooling at approximately 10°C/min will form coherent Ni3Ti-type nanoprecipitates.
The two-stage treatment will produce a nanostructure containing coherent Ni3Ti-type precipitates and matrix short-range-order clusters.
Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates can impede or trap moving dislocations.
The proposed coherent nanoprecipitates will refine the microstructure.
Short-range-order clusters create local variations in atomic bonding that facilitate controlled dislocation motion.
Short-range-order clusters blunt crack tips.
Combining an ordered precipitate structure with a ductile matrix can improve the strength-ductility balance.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 25% relative to an untreated or precipitate-free CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
The treatment will improve ductility by approximately 10% relative to an untreated or precipitate-free CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
The treatment will improve fracture toughness by approximately 20% relative to an untreated or precipitate-free CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
The treated alloy will retain a high Young's modulus.
An inert atmosphere is required to avoid oxidation during processing.
The beneficial response requires dopant levels below 3 at.%.
The beneficial microstructure requires service temperatures well below the order-disorder transition temperature.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration can coarsen the precipitates or dissolve the short-range-order clusters, eliminating the intended mechanical benefits.
In-situ TEM or DSC monitoring will permit precise control of the annealing process.
Mechanical testing and TEM or atom-probe tomography can measure the predicted properties and determine whether the proposed precipitates and short-range-order clusters formed.
The hypothesis is falsified only if the strength threshold and the ductility and toughness improvements are missed and the proposed dual microstructure is absent.
